_docs.aggregate_slow_handling: Alias-stability D3 (OPT-IN, docs/architecture/alias-stability-and-slow-engines.md): the :8800 slow-engine policy. 'wait' (DEFAULT) is today byte-for-byte — a slow engine is simply waited on, no timer installed. 'failover' arms a TTFB watchdog on the buffered ALIASED forward only: if no upstream response headers arrive within aggregate_ttfb_timeout_ms, the request is answered from the alias's published fallback_targets (pre-first-byte only, exactly ONE retry, the row token from the arbiter key plane, the body re-spliced to the fallback's engine_model). Anything invalid reads as 'wait'.
_docs.aggregate_ttfb_timeout_ms: The watchdog deadline in ms. Absent or 0 = OFF (even in failover mode both keys must agree). Cleared forever the moment ANY upstream response (even an error status) arrives — never a retry after the first byte.
_docs.aggregate_queue_depth_cap: Queue-suppression cap (default 3, read only in failover mode): when the watchdog fires and that engine's FRESH (<=20s) arbiter-published queue depth is > 0 and < this cap, the engine is demonstrably still working — the wait is extended (logged, repeatable) instead of failing over. Stale/zero/over-cap makes failover eligible.
_docs.config: Copy this file to client/config.json (untracked/local). Relative paths (queue_file, results_file) resolve against the client/ package dir — e.g. '../data/queue.jsonl' → <repo>/data/queue.jsonl.
_docs.executor: Command template run via bash -c. Placeholders: {payload_file}, {result_file}, and {repo} — expanded to the TRUE idlefill repo root in both layouts (dev: tsx client/src/index.ts; packaged: client/dist), so 'node {repo}/adapters/career-ops/eval.mjs …' finds the adapter at <repo>/adapters/career-ops/eval.mjs. At startup the client checks the expanded script path exists and refuses to request leases (staying registered/online-but-inactive, FATAL in the log) if it is missing — a broken executor template must not burn job attempts.
_docs.adapter: Alternative to hand-writing 'executor' (issue #13): name a registered adapter (e.g. "career-ops", "noop") and the client resolves the executor template, payload_fields, estimated_seconds, and timeout_seconds from its manifest at <repo>/adapters/<name>/package.json (the "idlefill" key). Precedence: an explicit 'executor' here wins over the manifest; an unknown adapter name is FATAL at startup (same online-but-inactive posture as a missing script). cwd stays config-only — it is machine-specific, never manifest material.
_docs.scheduled_rebuild: Issue #3: the daemon runs 'command' (a black box — the operator's own scan → refresh → queue-rebuild chain) on a minimum interval since the last run, checked on the poll tick. every_minutes defaults to 60 when enabled without it; the command runs via bash -c with the project's cwd and a 15-minute cap. Run state persists next to the queue file (<queue_file>.rebuild.json: last_run_ts, exit_code, duration_ms, queue_before/after) and rides the heartbeat to the dashboard as last_rebuild. Guards: one rebuild in flight per project; a nonzero exit records the failure and the daemon never touches the queue itself (empty-source refusal is the command's job). 'daily_at' is a known follow-up.
_docs.session_gate: Issue #9: the loopback proxy doubles as the router/gate for interactive agent traffic on /s/<token>/v1/... (register by first sight, capacity-limited FIFO admission, queued/paused requests HELD not failed, fail-open when the arbiter is down). true by default; false disables the gate (plain /v1/... job traffic is never gated either way). max_active_agent_sessions (default 2) = sessions holding the engine at once; session_hold_cap_ms (default 120000) = park limit before a retryable 503 + Retry-After — keep it well under the agent's own request timeout (Hermes: HERMES_API_TIMEOUT, default 1800s). Point a session at it with: /model http://127.0.0.1:11435/s/<token>
